Lemma
[The augmented equation has an invertible derivative at a simple eigenpair]

↗ def:augmented-eigen-equation ↗ def:eigen-linearisation ↗ def:simple-eigenpair ↗ lem:eigen-linearisation-injective

The map $\Phi _{v_0}$ is smooth, with derivative \[ D\Phi _{v_0}(S,v,\lambda )(T,w,\mu ) =\bigl(T,Tv+Sw-\lambda w-\mu v,\langle v_0,w\rangle \bigr). \] At a simple eigenpair satisfying $\langle v_0,v\rangle =1$, this derivative is a linear isomorphism.

Proof

↗ lem:eigen-linearisation-injective \sketch The formula follows by differentiating the polynomial components. Relative to $\operatorname {End}(V)\oplus (V\times \mathbb R)$, the derivative is block lower triangular with diagonal blocks $\operatorname {id}$ and $L_{S,v,\lambda ,v_0}$; both are invertible.

□
